summary: The proof is correct and complete. The affine map has rank two and is an affine isomorphism onto the coordinate-sum plane, so it preserves positivity of planar area. Boundary portions of the weak sign cells lie on finitely many lines and have zero area, justifying the selection of three affinely independent strict-chamber points. All three displayed lambda identities expand exactly as claimed; their strictly positive coefficients yield a strictly interior convex combination whose coordinates are all negative. The resulting nondegenerate triangle contains a planar neighborhood in the central chamber, proving positive central-cell area. Boundary and degeneracy cases are handled, and the prescribed calibration masses r_12=r_13=r_23=1 and r_123=0 contradict the proved universal implication in any convex common-plane realization.
